issues.detail: The Greek 'ο μη εχων' (the one who does not have) refers to the one without a money bag/pouch (βαλάντιον), not '沒有刀的' (the one without a sword). The Chinese adds '刀' (sword) which is not in the Greek at this point; the Greek says 'the one who does not have [a money bag]' should sell his cloak and buy a sword. This changes who is instructed to buy the sword.
